classification.difficultyReason: Differentiate a mass function, distinguish mass melted from mass remaining, and compare the magnitudes of rates.

content.prompt: A block of ice of mass 8 kg melts according to the formula $M=8-\dfrac{t^2}{32}$, where $M$ is the mass remaining, in kilograms, after $t$ minutes.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the time taken for all the ice to melt.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}0&=8-\frac{t^2}{32}\\t^2&=256\\t&=16\end{align*}$$
Time is non-negative, so all the ice melts after 16 minutes.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the rate at which the ice is melting after 4 minutes.

answer.short: $-0.25\text{ kg/min}$; the mass decreases by $0.25\text{ kg/min}$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{dM}{dt}&=-\frac{t}{16}\\\left.\frac{dM}{dt}\right|_{t=4}&=-\frac{4}{16}\\&=-0.25\text{ kg/min}\end{align*}$$
The mass is decreasing by $0.25\text{ kg/min}$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the rate at which the ice is melting when 2 kg of ice has melted.

answer.short: $-0.5\text{ kg/min}$; the mass decreases by $0.5\text{ kg/min}$.
answer.worked:
When 2 kg has melted, $M=8-2=6$ kg.
$$\begin{align*}6&=8-\frac{t^2}{32}\\t^2&=64\\t&=8\\\frac{dM}{dt}&=-\frac{t}{16}\\\left.\frac{dM}{dt}\right|_{t=8}&=-\frac{8}{16}\\&=-0.5\text{ kg/min}\end{align*}$$
The mass is decreasing by $0.5\text{ kg/min}$.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Is the melting rate faster initially, or just before it is gone completely?

answer.short: Faster just before it is gone completely.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\left.\frac{dM}{dt}\right|_{t=0}&=0\text{ kg/min}\\\left.\frac{dM}{dt}\right|_{t=16}&=-1\text{ kg/min}\end{align*}$$
Just before 16 minutes, the magnitude of the rate approaches $1\text{ kg/min}$, compared with zero initially. The ice therefore melts faster just before it is gone completely.
